title: The stage-two bump install (download, verify, install CI-built binaries, rewrite the digest map) is a scratchpad script, not a repository one
description: Ruled by opum-agent 2026-09-15 17:45Z after the 0.7.1 bump: land the stage-two script under scripts/ before the next bump. Stage two of a version bump (runbook "What a version bump touches") was hand steps at 0.7.0 and a session-scratchpad script at 0.7.1: gh run download of the six quest-package-<target> artifacts from a prepublication-qualification run, sha256 recomputed over each downloaded binary and compared to that artifact own questBinarySha256 before anything is installed, package.json/LICENSE/bin copied into npm/quest-<target>/, chmod +x, then root package.json questPlatformPackages rewritten to the same six digests. The runbook darwin-arm64 SIGKILL hazard applies: the script must never execute the downloaded binary, and the darwin-arm64 file must be the last thing recreated before git touches it. Repetition performed reliably by hand is still an automation gap.

acceptanceCriteria.text: scripts/install-platform-candidates.mjs (or equivalent name) takes a qualification run id, downloads the six artifacts, refuses on any digest mismatch before installing anything, installs manifests, LICENSE and binaries, and rewrites questPlatformPackages; it never executes a downloaded binary
A test or dry-run mode proves the refusal path: a tampered artifact stops the install with nothing written
The runbook stage-two text points at the script instead of describing hand steps, and package.json exposes it as a script
check:packages exits 0 after a run against a real qualification run id, verified on the PR

implementationNotes:
THE 0.7.1 SCRIPT, verbatim, so it outlives the session scratchpad it was written in. Ran once for real: six of six digests agreed, check:packages and test:packages exit 0 afterwards. It is POSIX sh plus node, python3 and gh; the repository version should be an .mjs under scripts/ with the same four phases and a tamper test.

#!/bin/sh
# Stage two of a bump: install the six CI-built platform packages from a
# prepublication-qualification run into npm/quest-<target>/, verifying each
# artifact's own questBinarySha256 against the downloaded bytes first, then
# write the same digests into root package.json's questPlatformPackages map.
# Usage: install-candidates.sh <run-id> <download-dir>   (run from the repo root)
set -eu
run="$1"; dir="$2"
rm -rf "$dir"; mkdir -p "$dir"
targets="darwin-arm64 darwin-x64 linux-arm64 linux-x64 win32-arm64 win32-x64"
for t in $targets; do
  gh run download "$run" --name "quest-package-$t" --dir "$dir/$t" >/dev/null
  case "$t" in win32-*) bin="quest.exe";; *) bin="quest";; esac
  expected="$(node -p "require('$dir/$t/package.json').questBinarySha256")"
  actual="$(shasum -a 256 "$dir/$t/bin/$bin" | cut -d' ' -f1)"
  version="$(node -p "require('$dir/$t/package.json').version")"
  if [ "$expected" != "$actual" ]; then
    echo "DIGEST MISMATCH for $t: manifest says $expected, bytes are $actual" >&2; exit 1
  fi
  echo "$t version=$version sha256=$actual (manifest agrees)"
done
echo "--- all six verified; installing"
for t in $targets; do
  case "$t" in win32-*) bin="quest.exe";; *) bin="quest";; esac
  cp "$dir/$t/package.json" "npm/quest-$t/package.json"
  cp "$dir/$t/LICENSE" "npm/quest-$t/LICENSE"
  rm -f "npm/quest-$t/bin/$bin"
  cp "$dir/$t/bin/$bin" "npm/quest-$t/bin/$bin"
  chmod +x "npm/quest-$t/bin/$bin"
done
python3 - "$dir" <<'PY'
import json, re, sys, hashlib, os
d=sys.argv[1]
p='package.json'; s=open(p).read()
for t in ["darwin-arm64","darwin-x64","linux-arm64","linux-x64","win32-arm64","win32-x64"]:
    digest=json.load(open(f"{d}/{t}/package.json"))["questBinarySha256"]
    pat=re.compile(r'("@opum-ai/quest-%s": ")[0-9a-f]{64}(")' % re.escape(t))
    s,n=pat.subn(r'\g<1>'+digest+r'\2', s)
    assert n==1, (t,n)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print("questPlatformPackages updated")
PY
